title: The 10 Best Cordless Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kits
subtitle: Two-tool drill and impact driver kits with batteries and charger, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A combo kit pairs a drill/driver with an impact driver, two batteries and a charger, the starter set for most cordless tool owners. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Milwaukee, Makita, Bosch, CRAFTSMAN and Greenworks on rating, review volume and features (brushless motors, two batteries, a 1/2-inch drill chuck and a bag or case). Choose the battery platform first; it decides which tools you can add later.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Cordless Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kit, 2 Batteries, Charger and Bag (DCK240C2)

specs.extras: Charger, bag; impact 5.55 in long, 2.8 lb

products.verdict: The best-selling and most-reviewed kit here by a mile, with 61,088 reviews: DEWALT's compact drill and impact driver with two batteries, a charger and a bag.
products.best_for: First-time buyers who want the most proven kit on the biggest battery platform.
products.skip_if: You want brushless motors; the DCK277D2 or a FUEL kit has them.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 MAX Cordless Drill and Impact Driver Kit, 2 Batteries, Charger (CMCK200C2)
products.verdict: A cheaper name-brand kit with a two-speed drill, a 1,460 in-lb impact driver, two batteries, a charger and a bag.
products.best_for: Homeowners on a budget who want a brand with a big tool lineup.
pros: Low price for a name brand

products.name: Greenworks 24V Brushless Drill/Driver and Impact Driver Combo, 2 x 2.0Ah USB-C Batteries

specs.extras: Batteries double as USB-C power banks

products.verdict: A brushless kit with a 400 in-lb drill and a 1,950 in-lb impact driver, plus two batteries that also work as USB-C power banks.
products.best_for: Greenworks yard-tool owners and budget buyers who want brushless.
products.skip_if: You want the biggest choice of add-on tools.
pros: Battery doubles as a power bank
cons: Smaller tool platform than DEWALT or Milwaukee

products.name: Milwaukee M12 FUEL 2-Tool Combo Kit (3404-20 Hammer Drill + Impact Driver)
products.verdict: Milwaukee's top 12V kit: a FUEL hammer drill and impact driver that are small enough for cabinets and tight spaces, rated 4.8 stars.
products.best_for: Remodelers, electricians and plumbers who value compact size.
products.skip_if: You'll drill big holes in masonry; an 18V kit is stronger.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL 2-Tool Combo Kit (Hammer Drill + Impact Driver)
products.verdict: Milwaukee's flagship 18V pair: brushless FUEL hammer drill and impact driver for heavy daily use, rated 4.8 stars.
products.best_for: Pros and serious DIYers who want top-end power.
products.skip_if: You're on a budget; it's among the priciest here.

products.name: Makita CT225SYX 18V LXT Compact Cordless 2-Pc Combo Kit (1.5Ah)
products.verdict: Makita's compact kit: a 3.3 lb, 7-1/4-inch 1/2-inch drill with 480 in-lb, an impact driver, two batteries and a charger, for Makita's huge 18V LXT lineup.
products.skip_if: You want brushless; the XT269T has it.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Drill and Impact Driver Kit with 2 x 2.0Ah Batteries (DCK277D2)
products.verdict: A step up from the DCK240C2 with larger 2.0Ah batteries, the 1,500 in-lb DCF787 impact driver, a contractor bag and a 3-year warranty.
products.best_for: DEWALT buyers who want more runtime than the entry kit.

products.name: BOSCH 12V Max Cordless 2-Tool Combo Kit, PS31 Drill/Driver and PS41 Impact Driver
products.verdict: A compact Bosch 12V pair for overhead work and tight spaces, with a 30-minute charger, soft case and 4.8 stars on almost 6,000 reviews.
products.skip_if: You need a 1/2-inch chuck or 18V power.

products.name: DEWALT XTREME 12V MAX Brushless Cordless Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kit (DCK221F2)

specs.tools: DCD701 3/8 in drill + DCF801 1/4 in impact driver

products.verdict: DEWALT's compact brushless 12V pair: a 3/8-inch drill with 15 clutch settings and an impact driver DEWALT says is 20% shorter than before.

products.name: Milwaukee 2892-22CT M18 Compact Brushless 2-Tool Combo Kit, Drill Driver/Impact Driver
products.verdict: A cheaper way onto Milwaukee M18 with brushless motors: a compact drill/driver and impact driver with two batteries.
products.best_for: Buyers who want Milwaukee M18 without paying for FUEL.
products.skip_if: You want the most power; the FUEL kit is stronger.

avoid.name: Cordless Impact Driver and Drill Combo Kit (Tool Only) Compatible with Dewalt 20V Max Battery, Up to 2300 In-lbs
avoid.flag: 'Combo kit' with no battery or charger; torque claim beats DEWALT's own
avoid.verdict: It's sold as a combo kit but includes no battery or charger, and claims more impact torque than DEWALT's own impact driver.
reasons: The listing says in bold that it does 'NOT INCLUDE BATTERY AND CHARGER, TOOL ONLY', while the title calls it a 'Combo Kit', which on the DEWALT, Milwaukee and Makita kits here means batteries and charger in the box.
It claims up to 2,300 in-lbs from the impact driver, versus 1,500 in-lb for DEWALT's DCF787 in the DCK277D2, on the same DEWALT batteries.
DEWALT's own DCK240C2 kit, with two batteries, a charger and a bag, has 61,088 reviews.

buyers_guide.a: A drill and an impact driver cover nearly every drilling and driving job, and the kit price usually costs less than the two tools and batteries bought separately. More importantly, it puts you on a battery platform you'll use for future tools.
Pick the one whose other tools you'll want. DEWALT 20V MAX, Milwaukee M18 and Makita 18V LXT have the widest ranges. CRAFTSMAN V20, RYOBI ONE+ and Greenworks 24V are cheaper with fewer pro tools.
12V tools are smaller and lighter, great for cabinets, electrical and overhead work. 18V/20V tools have more power for big holes, long screws and masonry.
Yes if you use the tools often: brushless motors run cooler, last longer and get more work per charge. For occasional home use, a brushed kit like the DCK240C2 is fine.

buyers_guide.q: What does a hammer drill add?
buyers_guide.a: A hammer mode pounds as it spins, for drilling small holes in brick and concrete. It's useful for anchors; for big masonry holes, use a rotary hammer.
